translations.source_sense_description: het langzaam oxideren van ijzerhoudende materialen

glosses: The deteriorated state of iron or steel as a result of moisture and oxidation; it consists mostly of iron(III) oxide (ferric oxide) and iron(II) oxide (ferrous oxide).

examples.text: The rust on my bicycle chain made cycling to work very dangerous.

glosses: A similar substance based on another metal.

examples.text: copper rust

glosses: A reddish-brown color.
A disease of plants caused by a reddish-brown fungus.
Damage caused to stamps and album pages by a fungal infection.
To oxidize, especially of iron or steel.

examples.text: The patio furniture had rusted in the wind-driven spray.
Your gold and silver have rusted, and their rust will be evidence against you and will eat your flesh like fire.

glosses: To cause to oxidize.

examples.text: The wind-driven spray had thoroughly rusted the patio furniture.

glosses: To be affected with the parasitic fungus called rust.

examples.text: I am sorry to say that, contrary to the majority, I have to report that the forage rusted rather badly.

glosses: To (cause to) degenerate in idleness; to make or become dull or impaired by inaction.

examples.text: Must I rust in Egypt? never more / Appear in arms, and be the chief of Greece?

glosses: Of a black cat or its fur, to turn rust-coloured following long periods of exposure to sunlight.

examples.text: It's very common for black cats to rust during the summer.

translations.source_sense_description: het langzaam oxideren van ijzerhoudende materialen

glosses: Produire de la rouille sur la surface d’un corps.

examples.text: Les mauvais chemins, et le passage des rivières, où plus d’une fois les fantassins furent dans l’eau jusqu’à la poitrine, avaient rouillé les armes, ruiné les vêtements et surtout les chaussures.
En les examinant, il s’aperçut que la poudre était mouillée et que la pluie avait rouillé les ressorts au point que les batteries ne jouaient plus.

glosses: Se couvrir de rouille (pour un objet en fer ou en acier).

examples.text: Le dessin des champs s’efface, les barques pourrissent, les outils rouillent.
Peu lui importe, si les épées rouillent, les chevaux engraissent, il n’a ni envie de chasse, ni de guerre.

glosses: Altérer, affaiblir par manque d’exercice.

examples.text: On ne saurait moins d’esprit que couvrait un grand usage du monde et de la meilleure compagnie, mais que sa retraite avait rouillé.
S’il n’a pas la chance d’avoir à sa portée quelque grand travail, il se rouille dans l’inaction et le découragement en comparant les efforts qu’il a faits aux résultats obtenus.

glosses: Donner à des végétaux la teinte de la rouille.

examples.text: … il entre dans les dortoirs, quand les croisées sont ouvertes, des échos de feuillages et des tressaillements de nature déjà rouillée par l’automne, avec des tons chauds de bronze et de cuivre.

Grands bois, je vous verrai brillants sous un ciel d’ambre
Ou de molles vapeurs noyés ;
Je vous verrai si fiers quand le triste novembre
Vous aura meurtris et rouillés.
Le travail de récolte, en effet, ne se faisait point partout aussi rondement qu’au Paridier : de beaux blés restaient sur pied, rouillaient sous les averses et menaçaient de s’égrener.

examples.text: Das Fahrradschloss rostet nicht so schnell ein, wenn man es gut ölt.

glosses: unbeweglich/steif sein, weil man sich zu wenig bewegt hat unsicher/zögerlich/unflexibel sein, weil man etwas länger nicht getan hat

examples.text: Nach der Sommerpause fühlte sie sich ganz eingerostet. Gut, dass die abendlichen Workouts wieder losgehen sollten.
Wer sich nicht mehr um Neuerungen und Veränderungen schert, rostet schneller ein, als gleichaltrige Senioren.

examples.text: The UPS package centre for central London, a brief walk from Kentish Town tube station, holds a below-ground bay in which 170 vans roost every night.

glosses: To kick (a ball) a long distance.
Alternative form of roust (“strong tide or current”).

examples.text: Sometimes the whole tract swung to one side, like the tail of a live serpent; sometimes, for a glimpse, it would all disappear and then boil up again. What it was I had no guess, which for the time increased my fear of it; but I now know it must have been the roost or tide race, which had carried me away so fast and tumbled me about so cruelly, and at last, as if tired of that play, had flung out me and the spare yard upon its landward margin.

glosses: Alternative form of roust.

glosses: Any of the three species of spiny-finned freshwater fish in the genus Perca.
Any of the about 200 related species of fish in the taxonomic family Percidae, especially:
Acanthopagrus berda
Any of the about 200 related species of fish in the taxonomic family Percidae, especially:
Distichodus engycephalus, Distichodus rostratus
Any of the about 200 related species of fish in the taxonomic family Percidae, especially:
Johnius belangerii, Macquaria ambigua, Macquaria colonorum, Macquaria novemaculeata, Nemadactylus macropterus
Any of the about 200 related species of fish in the taxonomic family Percidae, especially:
Kyphosus azureus
Any of the about 200 related species of fish in the taxonomic family Percidae, especially:
Lateolabrax japonicus, Tautogolabrus adspersus
Several similar species in the order Perciformes, such as the grouper.
A rod, staff, tree branch, ledge, etc., used as a roost by a bird.

examples.text: We know him now: […] / Not making his high place the lawless perch / Of wing'd ambitions, nor a vantage-ground / For pleasure; […]

glosses: A pole connecting the fore gear and hind gear of a spring carriage; a reach.
A position that is secure and advantageous, especially one which is prominent or elevated.

examples.text: Last year, Eighth Grade found poignancy and humor in its eponymous time period: that purgatorial perch between childhood and adulthood.
[W]inning Wimbledon at just 19 years, earning her rightful place on the perch as world number one.

glosses: A position that is overly elevated or haughty.

examples.text: You may thanke me, (Lady) / I haue taken you off your mellancholly pearch, / Boare you vpon my fiſt, and ſhew'd you game, / And let you flie at it: I pray the kiſſe me, […]

glosses: A linear measure of 5+¹⁄₂ yards, equal to a rod, a pole or ¹⁄₄ chain; the related square measure.
A cubic measure of stonework equal to 16.6 × 1.5 × 1 feet.
A frame used to examine cloth.
A bar used to support a candle, especially in a church.
A platform for lights to be directed at the stage.
To rest on a perch (especially, of a bird); to roost.

examples.text: The macaw perched on Jim's shoulder.

glosses: To sit upon the edge of something.

examples.text: The platform was already crowded, but the newcomers threaded their way to the front amid a decorous murmur of welcome. Mr. Peeble shoved and exhorted and two end seats emerged upon which Enid and Malone perched themselves.

glosses: To stay in an elevated position.
To place something on (or as if on) a perch.

examples.text: The most obvious beneficiary of the visitors' superiority was Frank Lampard. By the end of the night he was perched 13th in the list of England's most prolific goalscorers, having leapfrogged Sir Geoff Hurst to score his 24th and 25th international goals. No other player has managed more than the Chelsea midfielder's 11 in World Cup qualification ties, with this a display to roll back the years.

glosses: To inspect cloth using a perch.

translations.source_sense_description: (kippen) op stok zitten

glosses: Se poser sur une perche, sur une branche d’arbre, sur une baguette, etc.

examples.text: Les coqs et les poules perchent toutes les nuits.
Quantité d’oiseaux sont venus percher sur ces arbres.
Un rossignol est venu se percher sur cette branche.

glosses: Se mettre sur quelque endroit élevé, pour mieux voir ou pour mieux entendre.

examples.text: Comment est-il allé percher, se percher là ?

glosses: Demeurer, se trouver.

examples.text: Où est-ce que tu perches ?
Il y avait un hôpital militaire, bricolé dans une école, ça pouvait aussi bien percher au pôle Nord que chez les Zoulous.

glosses: Produire son effet, en parlant d’un stupéfiant puissant.
Manipuler la perche pour la prise du son.
